reflection.text:
Unblinding: MG-132, truth Protein degradation (proteasome inhibitor). We submitted Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.68 then 0.58. Incorrect.

What we got right / should have weighted:
- Low-dose morphology pointed away from direct tubulin-targeting. e2 at 1 uM rep1 (103 cells): cell_roundness z=-26.4, cell_solidity z=-26.3, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+16.2. e5 at 0.3 uM rep1 (63 cells): frac_large_nucleus z=+15.3, act_std z=+14.9, nuc_major_axis z=+13.6. e11 dose-response for frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.95 p=0.051 across 4 wells/4 doses was borderline and consistent with enlarged nuclei/cell-cycle arrest, not classic stabilizer mitotic arrest.
- Atlas was unstable by dose, which we underweighted. e7 at 1 uM: DNA replication 5/10, DNA damage 2/10, Kinase inhibitors 2/10. e15: Eg5 inhibitors 4/10, Protein degradation 2/10, DNA replication 2/10. e16: Microtubule destabilizers 4/10, Epithelial 3/10. Only e12 at 3 uM gave Microtubule stabilizers 7/10. That dose-dependence should have raised uncertainty rather than confidence.
- Protein degradation was never absent: e7 2/10, e12 1/10, e15 2/10 for Protein degradation. It stayed at p=0.08 in both hypothesis updates (steps 13 and 19) but we did not pursue it. describe_phenotype e6 (4 fields: density lower vs DMSO, candidates: none) was non-diagnostic and should have kept the differential broad.
- Dose-responses were underpowered and contaminated. e8 rho=-0.80 p=0.2, e9 rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e10 rho=+0.40 p=0.6, e17 rho=-0.20 p=0.8 all n=1/dose, non-significant, and included the 30 uM well e3 (410 cells, nuc_solidity z=-414.8, act_tub_ratio z=-159.3) which is cytotoxic/artefactual. We interpreted e10 cell_count lack of monotonic loss as cytostatic vs cytotoxic without excluding that point.

What misled us and why:
- Single-well dominance. Conclusion rested on e4 dose 4, 3 uM rep1: 39 cells, tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.7, tub_mean z=+54.7, cell_solidity z=+30.5, paired with e12 7/10 stabilizer atlas (mean 0.83 we noted vs 0.62 at 1 uM). With 39 cells remaining, extreme z-scores likely reflect selective survival/bundling, not a primary target effect. The review critique was correct: abrupt 1->3 uM reversal (negative roundness/solidity at 1 uM to highly positive at 3 uM) could be single-well artefact, 0.68 overcalibrated.
- Acquisition choice under budget. Steps 1-5 used all 4/4 wells as n=1 across 0.3, 1, 3, 30 uM with no replicate. We then could not execute the review-requested experiment: acquire dose index 4 (3.0 uM) rep2 + atlas comparison to test reproducibility of high tub_mean/tub_glcm_contrast. Step 19 lowering to 0.58 acknowledged single-well risk but retained the call.
- Chemical prior absent. e21/e22 lookup MG-132 CID 462382, mechanisms: none curated, name/BBBC021 structure agree. So we relied entirely on image atlas, where proteasome inhibition is known to produce secondary cytoskeletal stabilization that mimics stabilizers.
- Literature integration was post-hoc. e23 search MG-132 proteasome inhibitor had 903 hits (PMID 21499287, PMID 30695709, PMID 18435911, PMID 21203833 confirm MG-132 is a proteasome inhibitor) and e24 proteasome inhibitor microtubule stabilization phenotype had 7 hits. These searches occurred after the second submission (steps 21-24) and could not inform the blinded call. Biologically, proteasome inhibition stabilizes many ubiquitinated regulators including microtubule-associated proteins, increasing tubulin intensity and texture (high tub_mean, high GLCM contrast) as a downstream phenotype, which explains e4/e12 without direct tubulin binding. Without citation, the lesson is to treat extreme tubulin texture/intensity with divergent low-dose nuclear enlargement as a flag for upstream protein-turnover stress rather than direct stabilizer.

If this were a real lab, the discriminating follow-up is not the acetylated-tubulin/pHH3/docetaxel control we proposed, but proteasome activity (e.g., chymotrypsin-like) and ubiquitin accumulation dose-response versus docetaxel/epothilone B, excluding the 30 uM cytotoxic point and requiring replicate 3 uM wells.

No clinical implications are inferred from this screening assay.

Without citation, the lesson is to treat extreme tubulin texture/intensity with divergent low-dose nuclear enlargement as a flag for upstream protein-turnover stress rather than direct stabilizer.

If this were a real lab, the discriminating follow-up is not the acetylated-tubulin/pHH3/docetaxel control we proposed, but proteasome activity (e.g., chymotrypsin-like) and ubiquitin accumulation dose-response versus docetaxel/epothilone B, excluding the 30 uM cytotoxic point and requiring replicate 3 uM wells.

No clinical implications are inferred from this screening assay.

What was right:
- e5 + e11 large-nucleus signal at low dose
- e7/e15/e16 atlas instability with Protein degradation neighbours present but downweighted
- e8-e11, e17 dose-responses non-significant n=1/dose including 30 uM artefact e3

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighting e4 3 uM rep1 39 cells tub_glcm_contrast +151.7 tub_mean +54.7 and e12 7/10 stabilizers as primary MoA
- Ignoring opposite e2 1 uM roundness/solidity negative and e7 DNA replication 5/10
- No replicate of 3 uM; budget 4/4 spent, review-requested rep2 not acquired
- Contaminating dose-response with 30 uM e3

Proposed next experiment: Proteasome functional orthogonal assay: dose-response for chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity and total poly-ubiquitin western/IF plus ubiquitin IF, vs tubulin control, excluding cytotoxic 30 uM well and requiring independent 3 uM replicate.
